propositions: Existing agent guidance does not document safe ChatGPT workflows when the tracker worktree is inaccessible or network/binary resources are unavailable, leading to unsafe ticket-creation attempts or incomplete handoffs.

The import mechanism silently drops records missing ticket_id/ticket_type without incrementing any counter or warning in dry-run mode, making malformed payloads invisible unless detected by comparing would_create + skipped against total record count.

Agents lack precise capability-check rules to determine when native ticket creation is impossible and should fall back to generating a reviewable export-schema payload instead of claiming persistence.

The fallback payload schema must conform to export.schema.json's required fields (schema_version, ticket_id, ticket_type, title, status) with agent-generated UUID4 ticket_id, which becomes source_id on import and enables idempotent re-ingestion.

Documentation must teach that rebar import (via CLI or library) is the only sanctioned exceptional ingest path—never raw event-file injection or GitHub Contents API writes—and must specify its actual dry-run behavior precisely.

A test suite must verify that AGENTS.md links to ChatGPT guidance, the guide prohibits GitHub Issues as a tracker substitute, rejects Contents-API writes as normal, names rebar import as the exclusive exceptional path, and matches export.schema.json's required fields.
